J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.10,50,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 1.1.2018 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-K-4882 on B.M. near Durgamma Temple, Shikaripura Taluk,
bearing registration No.KA- 42-M-9892 driven by its driver same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to Government hospital, Shikaripura,
wherein she took the first aid treatment, later on she was shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient for 20 days and underwent surgery.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident she was hale and healthy,
aged about 48 years, working as a teacher at GLPS Shattihalli, and getting salary of Rs.32,376/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15- X-7741.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and filed their written statements.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Further contended that this respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle and insured with the second respondent and policy was issued, policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

6. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:

2
The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that driver of the car had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the manner of the accident, involvement of the vehicle.
Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act.
This respondent has denied about the issuance of policy to the alleged vehicle bearing No.KA- 42-M-9892.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner, if he would have taken care and caution while riding the moped, the accident would not have occurred.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against it with cost.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741 on 1.1.2018 at about 9.30 p.m. near Durgamma Temple, Kotta Village, Shikripura Taluk, Shimogga District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
8.

In order to prove the case, the petitioner herself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 and Ex.P20 & Ex.P21 marked with consent and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.
9.
To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not examined any witness on their behalf.

10. Heard the arguments.
11.

My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3:

sentences.text: 12 . ISSUE NO.1:-
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved her case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents have argued that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondents.
14. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
15. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and she has stated in her evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of her evidence, she has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P1 to ExP6 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
16.
On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by petitioner on 1.1.12018.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Shikaripura Rural Police in Cr. No.2/2018 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15- X-7741 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex . P2 and Ex.P3 are the spot mahazar and sketch reveals that the alleged incident was taken place and it corroborate the version of PW1.
On perusal of Ex.P4-IMV report also reveals that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex. P5
is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P6 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.

17. The counsel for the respondents have argued that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the petitioner and not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741.
To substantiate the said fact the respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence in order to prove its case.
On the other hand the petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

entities.text: 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 1.1.2018 at about 9.30 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Shikaripura,
The doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which shows that he was admitted on 2.1.2018 and discharged on 22.1.2018 and underwent open reduction internal fixation with TBW for right patella,
open reduction internal fixation with LCP for right tibial condyle and wound debridement right leg done.
She has produced another discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, which shows that the petitioner was admitted on 23.7.2018 and discharged on 25.7.2018 for implant removal and debridement of right leg.
She has produced outpatient record atEx.P13, lab report at Ex.P14, copy of driving license at Ex.P15, copy of Aadhar card at Ex.P16 and x-rays at Ex.P17.

22 . PW2 being the Orthopaedic Surgeon has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and treated with ORIF with Tension band wiring for the right patella, ORIF with LCP for right tibial condyle, wound debridement shortening and closure right toe on 5.1.2018, she underwent wound debridement of the right leg.
He has produced the documents marked at Ex.18 and Ex.P19 such as case sheet and x-rays.

23. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
24. The case of the petitioner is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 48 years, working as a Teacher at GLPS Shattihalli getting salary of Rs.33,376/- per month.
The petitioner has produced pay slips marked at Ex.P9 for the months of May 2018, June 2018 and December 2017.
On perusal of the same she was getting salary of Rs.32,376/- per month.
She ahs also produced bank statement at Ex.P11.
On perusal of Ex.P9 and Ex.P11, she was getting salary of Rs.33,376/- per month.
On perusal of attendance register marked at Ex.P11, which shows that the petitioner has not attended the duty from January 1-1-2018 till April 30th.
After that she has attended for duty on 2nd July and again she has applied leave from 12th July to 9th August.
In her cross-examination she has stated that for removal of implants again she has admitted for the hospital.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which shows that he was admitted on 2.1.2018 and discharged on 22.1.2018 and again she was admitted for removal of implants.

To substantiate the said fact, she has produced another discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, which shows that the petitioner was admitted on 23.7.2018 and discharged on 25.7.2018 for implant removal and debridement of right leg.
But the petitioner has not examined the doctor nor produced any documents to shows that due to the accidental injuries she requires five months leave.
Any how considering the nature of the injuries she might have taken rest and treatment atleast for three months.

Therefore, three months income comes to Rs.1,00,128/- is granted to the petitioner Smt. Karibasamma vs Shri Hanumanthappa on 4 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197910134/
5 under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
25. The contention of the petitioner is that, she has spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses.
On record she has produced the medical bills at Ex.P12 to the extent of Rs.3,16,278/- .

So,
considering the evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.3,16,278/- under the head of medical expenses.
26. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 48 years.
Due to severe injuries she is permanently disabled.
As I have already discussed that the petitioner is working as a Teacher and getting salary of Rs.32,376/- , so she has continued the same job.
At this juncture the counsel for the respondent has relied the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in between Shri Subash Vs. The New India Assurance Co.Ltd., rep. by its Manager and others,

entities.text: Shri Subash Vs. The New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the above decision, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.

27. At this juncture I relied the decision of our Hon'ble High Court reported in ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others, in which it is held that;
 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988---Section  173(1)---Accident claim---Judgment and  Award--- Appealed against ---Claim for enchancement of compensation---Respondent- appreciation of evidence on record---- Assessment of disability to the whole body--- Courts to add a suitable sum by way of damages having regard to degree of physical handicap---HELD, The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.

entities.text: Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labour market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre-accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers, this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first.

28. On perusal of the said decision, it is observed that though the claimant is in a position to work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.

Since the Smt. Karibasamma vs Shri Hanumanthappa on 4 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197910134/
6 claimant is continuing in his employment, he may not be entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to his disability.

entities.text: Smt. Karibasamma vs Shri Hanumanthappa on 4 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 29. In the instant case, the petitioner has sustained right patella transverse fracture, right bicondylar fracture, proximal tibia crush injury great toe with nail bed loss.
Due to this injury PW2 doctor has assessed the disability to the extent of 14% to the whole body.

Though the petitioner has continued her service, she has to suffer with the said disability throughout her life and her eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

So,
suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.
30. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
So her happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out her life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of amenities.
31. PW1 has stated in her evidence that due to the accident she took the treatment as inpatient and also as outpatient and due to the injuries she is completely deformed.
On perusal of discharge summary at Ex.P8, it appears that, the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 2.1.2018 to 22.1.2018.
Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, so, one must attend her for the period of hospitalization and rest period.

Therefore, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
32.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No.
Compensation heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 1,00,128-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.3,16,278-00 4.
Reduced eligibility of employment Rs.1,00,000-00 or damages due to disability 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 25,000-00 6.
Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 25,000-00 conveyance charges Rs.6,16,406-00 33.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741.

Smt. Karibasamma vs Shri Hanumanthappa on 4 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197910134/
7 34.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer has not admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-15-X-7741 and its validity.
But on perusal of the cause title of the claim petition, the validity of the policy is from 11.5.2017 to 10.5.2018.
The accident occurred on 1.1.2018.
From this it is clear that the policy is valid as on the date of accident.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the issuance of the policy and its validity, but has not challenged the same.
From this it is clear that as on the date of accident the policy was in existence.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation together with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of IMV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,16,406/- with interest @8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest at 8%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized/scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 4th day of April 2019).
(MAHANTESH S.DARGAD) III ADDL.SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & XXIX ACMM, BANGALORE.
